newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse spinoff hailed by debt holders.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse spinoff hailed by debt holders.

text.p: Bondholders breathed a sigh of relief after Westinghouse Electric Corp announced on Wednesday that it will retain over $2 billion of public debt on its balance sheet after spinning off its industrial business, trading sources said.
"The market was anticipating the spin-off, but the question was who will the debt end up with," said one trader.
"On the whole the market has given its vote of confidence to the idea of lumping the debt with the broadcasting assets which have great cash flow," he added.

Another factor that boosted investor sentiment on the bonds was a decision by Standard & Poor's Corp to revise the outlook of the double-B corporate credit rating of Westinghouse to "positive" from "developing," the trader said.
He noted spreads on Westinghouse debt had tightened by 10 to 15 basis points by midday.
In the broader market, prices on high-grade bonds tracked Treasuries, while the high-yield bond market outperformed the Treaury market as of midday.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was down 16/32 at 100-8/32 at midday.
